name: WA-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Rick Larsen seeking re-election with large financial edge
No polls or expert ratings; challenger underfunded and little known
Prediction markets price Democratic win around 96%
model.rationale: Larsen combines a D+12 district, incumbency, and a roughly $2 million warhead against an underfunded challenger, and markets price his re-election near certain. With no polls to refine the estimate, the margin rests on fundamentals and stays near the district's structural lean.
model.watch: Any late polling or unexpected outside spending on Feller's behalf would be the first sign the race is competitive.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Rick Larsen, a Democratic incumbent first elected in 2000, is seeking another term in a northwestern Washington district that leans about twelve points Democratic. He has raised more than $2 million and holds a large cash advantage, while Republican challenger Edwin Feller has reported minimal fundraising and no outside support. No general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race.

Prediction markets give Larsen roughly a 96% chance of winning, consistent with the district's fundamentals and his incumbency. The race is rated Safe Democratic, though the absence of polling means the exact margin carries meaningful uncertainty.
